mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital costs decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the following 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by >0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% monthly indicate robust consumer and business demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained earnings expansion.
failure_condition: The joint signal of GDPC1 and HOUST fails to correlate with positive 60-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 0.3% monthly signals manufacturing resilience that supports corporate margins, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not produce positive 20-day SPX returns in late-cycle expansion (Rank IC < 0.05) over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate increases above 4.0% trigger aggressive monetary tightening that elevates discount rates for equity valuation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% monthly reflects labor market health that increases consumer spending and corporate revenue, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery regimes, rising residential fixed investment (RSAFS) above 0.3% monthly indicates housing demand recovery that stimulates economic growth and equity market performance, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in post-recession recovery (Rank IC < 0.05) over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 0.3% and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% monthly indicate supply-driven inflation that triggers rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO and CPIAUCSL both increase by >0.5% monthly.
